children: none, because the fix is one reader, one guard, and the fixtures that encode the old contract — a single component, a single seam. The lane-fate question inside it is a decision the build makes with reasoning recorded, not a separable piece of work with its own falsifier.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-roster-fault-is-one-finding) -> [PROVED]

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the run's total finding count, the roster-fault count, and whether the derivation command resolved
watchme.consumer: whoever next reads `cairnmap --gate`, and the IOU scrub that found this (an-iou-notices-when-its-physics-arrives is its sibling from the same idea)
watchme.enough: 10 gate runs across at least 3 distinct corpus states (a skill added, a skill removed, the node class edited) with the roster fault never appearing more than once per run. Fewer runs than that and a green reads as 'the corpus did not move', which is the shape of the historical-fact green this system keeps catching.
watchme.nexus: cairnmap's own tree — the surface that learns whether its findings are real
watchme.trigger: each `cairnmap --gate` run over the live corpus — the gate is the thing being watched, so its own firing is the trigger; no clock, no daemon
